record.title: KGBDCNet: keyword-guided building damage captioning network for bi-temporal remote sensing images
record.abstract: Building damage captioning is an emerging task within damage extraction, playing a crucial role in damage assessment and decision-making tasks. However, the complexity of disaster-affected environments and the diversity of damage manifestations make it challenging for current models to accurately identify damage features and generate comprehensive captions. To advance the development of building damage captioning and improve caption accuracy, this study constructed a dataset namedBD-CCand proposed a building damage feature keyword-guided caption model (KGBDCNet). In terms of dataset, the BD-CC dataset focuses on building damage in the Mariupol region, collecting a total of 4300 pairs of high-resolution RGB dual-temporal remote sensing images obtained from Google Earth. This includes 2877 pairs of images showing damaged buildings and 1423 pairs showing undamaged buildings, with all damage resulting from human conflict. Regarding the model, this paper utilizedLoRAto fine-tune theRemote-CLIPfor efficient extraction multi-modal features of damaged buildings. To fuse multi-modal features, this paper designed thecross-modal attention guided module (CAGM), which employs aretrieve-enhance strategyto guide damage keywords to enhance the visual feature representation of damage information. This paper further proposed thespatial–temporal memory-enhanced module (STMEM), which significantly improves the model’s recognition accuracy for changed regions and its ability to capture temporal evolution by establishing the dynamic associations of spatial–temporal features between bi-temporal images. The benchmarked experiment of the BD-CC dataset was conducted using current state-of-the-art methods to validate its effectiveness. On the public datasetLEVIR-CCand the self-built datasetBD-CC, comparison experiments were conducted betweenKGBDCNetand other methodsto test the model’s advancement. Additionally, we integrated alarge language modeland damaged grade judgement criteria to achievezero-shot building damage assessmentbased on the captions generated by the model, testing itsrobustness and generalizability. In the aforementioned experiments, the proposed method achieved superior results, demonstrating its effectiveness. The code of the proposed method will be made available at https://github.com/Lucky-DW/KGBDCNet.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: Causally regularized full-resolution channel attention and frequency refinement for cloud removal in satellite imagery
record.abstract: Optical remote sensing images are essential for Earth surface analysis; however, their applications are limited by cloud occlusion, as annual global cloud coverage exceeds 60%. The introduction of temporal compensation has addressed the limitation of single-image approaches, which struggled with thick cloud cover. The integration of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data has further improved their cloud removal performance. Nevertheless, existing methods still face notable challenges. Specifically, they lack fine-grained, long-range compensation and adaptive mechanisms to effectively distinguish the high-frequency information from noise. Moreover, current approaches lack an optimization mechanism to ensure the acquisition of the most representative features. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel Optical–SAR fusion method for cloud removal that explicitly combines controlled spatio–temporal aggregation with causal regularization (CR). A pixel-wise channel attention (PCA) module with high-frequency refinement (HRR) is introduced to enable full-resolution feature extraction while introducing frequency compensation advantages under acceptable computational complexity. Temporal attention aggregation is applied to facilitate effective temporal compensation. Furthermore, the CR module is employed to suppress statistically correlated but semantically irrelevant features arising from Optical–SAR fusion and temporal aggregation, improving robustness and generalization. Extensive experiments on both simulated and real-world datasets confirm the effectiveness of the proposed spatio–temporal feature extraction architecture, showing measurable yet modest metric improvements and state-of-the-art generalization under realistic cloud contamination. https://github.com/wjven/CR-PCA-HRR.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: MSENet: multi-task synergistic enhancement network for 3D building instance change detection
record.abstract: 3D building instance change detection enables the monitoring of changes in individual building entities, serving as a critical means for security warning and urban management. Existing methods typically adopt a ​​multi-stage approach​​ based on multiple independent task-specific models to sequentially address instance segmentation and change detection in a decoupled manner. However, these methods not only increase computational complexity but also struggle to leverage the synergistic relationships among multiple tasks to enhance change detection performance. Furthermore, existing change detection datasets lack instance-level annotations, which impedes the development of deep learning-based 3D instance change detection methods.​ Thereby, we expand upon existing 3D point cloud change detection datasets by introducing new building instance labels, resulting in a publicly available urban 3D Building instance Change Detection dataset, named 3DBiCD. It integrates photogrammetric and LiDAR point clouds to characterize 3D building instance change across Hong Kong, China, and Utrecht, Netherlands, with 10,501 building instances, of which 2044 instances change, exhibiting a 19.5% change ratio. Moreover, we propose a Multi-task Synergistic Enhancement Network, named MSENet, which achieves end-to-end 3D building instance change detection in a single-stage approach and leverages inter-task synergy to enhance change detection performance. Specifically, it integrates two innovative modules, the Instance Cluster Mask (ICM)module and the Instance-oriented Change Refinement (ICR)module, to unify instance segmentation and change detection within a single framework. The ICM module processes change-rich encoded features through a clustering-guided feature fusion approach to output precise instance masks​, and the ICR module integrates the instance-specific geometric and semantic cues to refine foreground instance change features. Experiments show that MSENet achieves 83.06% and 92.54% of the mean of IoU over building changes on realistic point clouds, leading to an improvement of 3.97% and 2.87% over the state-of-the-art, demonstrating the efficiency of MSENet. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/zhanwenxiao/MSENet and https://github.com/zhanwenxiao/3DBiCD.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: DHT-SWNet: Frequency-aware ship and wake detection in multi-source optical remote sensing imagery
record.abstract: This study addresses automatic detection of ship wakes in optical remote-sensing images, aiming to improve accuracy and efficiency via joint detection of ships and Kelvin wakes. First, we construct a new Remote Sensing Ship Wake (RSSW) dataset from multi-source optical imagery and develop dedicated labeling software to ensure reliable data preparation. Second, we propose the Discrete Hartley Transform Ship Wake Network (DHT-SWNet), which integrates DHT-based frequency analysis to capture the characteristic patterns of Kelvin wake. To further enhance representation, the network adopts efficient multi-scale feature integration, strengthening learning across different spatial scales. Experimental results show that the method achieves 75.63% mAP for wake detection, outperforming representative deep-learning baselines. The system simultaneously localizes ships and wakes on wide-area optical images, providing an effective tool for maritime surveillance, environmental protection, and ship navigation, and supporting subsequent ocean monitoring and analysis.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: IMEA-Net: An edge-sensitive network for cropland change detection in high-resolution remote sensing images
record.abstract: Cropland resources are experiencing substantial pressure due to the combined effects of global climatic shifts and population growth. Meanwhile, the extensive trend of “cropland conversion” has intensified the loss of cropland, threatening food stability. To tackle this issue, remote sensing has emerged as a crucial approach for observing changes in cropland. However, recognizing changes in cropland using high-resolution remote sensing imagery is still a difficult task because of challenges such as large intra-class variation and small inter-class variation of cropland in complex contexts, insufficient extraction of detail at the edges of cropland, and insufficient optimization stability under imbalanced sample conditions. In response to these challenges, we propose an innovative cropland change detection network, IMEA-Net. Firstly, an intelligent weighted wavelet signal extractor (IWWSE) is introduced to extract low-frequency global background and high-frequency local detail features of cropland from remote sensing images using wavelet transform. Secondly, a novel edge-sensitive mamba (ESMamba) is proposed to enhance the detection of fuzzy boundaries of cropland through spatial modeling and structural adjustment. Finally, an adaptive fusion optimization algorithm (AFOA) is introduced to enhance training stability by dynamically adjusting the learning rate. The experimental evaluation confirms that IMEA-Net outperforms seven state-of-the-art (SOTA) approaches on six benchmark datasets: CLCD, LuojiaSET-CLCD, Hi-CNA, JL1, Fuzhou and PX-CLCD. Furthermore, in practical applications, 50 high-resolution image pairs are collected by the Google Earth API. The results demonstrate that IMEA-Net effectively captures cropland changes and shows promising generalization performance.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: GEOIMIA: A new automated forest thinning framework for selective harvesting at the individual tree level in mixed-species forests
record.abstract: Accurate characterization of individual tree attributes and spatial distributions is pivotal for scientifically guided forest thinning decisions, yet traditional methods for identifying target trees are subjective and labor-intensive. To address these challenges within the context of typical Chinese fir (Cunninghamia lanceolata) plantations in southern China, we propose a Geographic Object-based Integrated Multi-module Image Analysis (GEOIMIA) framework, incorporating three interconnected modules. First, an object-based classification module applies heuristic sequential optimization to achieve high object-level accuracy (97% on the validation set) for four categories—Chinese fir, broadleaf trees, other tree species, and others—across entire images, thereby enabling precise global semantic masks and robust species delineation. Second, we developed a dedicated detection network, AMC-Net, tailored to high-resolution UAV remote sensing data under low illumination conditions, enabling precise crown detection for Chinese fir with AP50 = 96.3% and AP50-95 = 58.3%. Model compression experiments further reduced AMC-Net’s parameters to 1.1 million (only 45.8% of the original) while maintaining comparable detection performance (APweighted = 62.1%). Third, a decision module supported by Maskable Proximal Policy Optimization (Maskable PPO) dynamically optimizes thinning priorities, effectively balancing canopy closure (CC), stem density (SD), and stand stability (SS) in real-time. Adhering to the Regulations for forest tending (GB/T15781–2015), this module implements selective thinning strategies that remove denser, smaller, or weaker trees and retain those with higher ecological and silvicultural value. Consequently, GEOIMIA offers an economical, efficient, and scalable solution for automated thinning operations in mixed-species forests.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: CCFA-Net: Cross-domain collaborative and foreground-aware for UAV object detection in hazy scenes
record.abstract: Accurate object detection for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is critical for a wide range of applications. However, hazy environments substantially degrade image quality, thereby diminishing the performance of conventional detectors and posing significant challenges for real-world deployment. Although existing approaches typically employ cascaded joint learning pipelines, the inherent functional discrepancy between low-level dehazing and high-level detection often leads to suboptimal performance. Consequently, achieving effective task coordination while maintaining robust detection accuracy in hazy UAV scenarios remains a key challenge. To address these issues, we propose a cross-domain collaborative and foreground-aware network (CCFA-Net) for enhanced UAV object detection under hazy conditions. Within a multi-task joint learning framework, we introduce a cross-domain collaborative dehazing decoder (CCDD) that integrates the dehazing process into the detector’s feature learning, enabling better task coordination and producing high-quality dehazed representations that further improve the discriminability of detection features. Moreover, to mitigate the potential negative impact of imperfect dehazing, we introduce a cross-domain feature fusion module (CFFM) that adaptively fuses the original hazy and dehazed features, achieving cross-domain complementarity and semantic enhancement. Additionally, considering UAV-specific challenges, a multi-scale foreground-aware module (MFAM) is developed to strengthen the representation of foreground objects across varying scales through multi-scale feature modeling and foreground-aware attention mechanisms. Extensive experiments on the HazyDet dataset demonstrate that CCFA-Net outperforms state-of-the-art methods, including DeCoDet, by 3.1% in mAP, achieving an overall mean Average Precision (mAP) of 54.6%. These results validate its effectiveness under challenging hazy UAV scenarios. The code will be publicly available at https://github.com/XFCV26/CCFA-Net.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: FD-SC: focus-diffusion self-contrastive framework empowers efficient remote sensing building damage detection
record.abstract: Efficient building damage detection (BDD) based on remote sensing images is crucial for rapid and accurate disaster assessment. However, existing methods struggle to balance accuracy and inference efficiency, and depend heavily on large amounts of annotated data. This conflicts with the demands for high precision, high time sensitivity, and limited resources in actual disaster scenarios. To address these challenges, this study proposes the Focus-Diffusion Self-Contrastive (FD-SC) framework, which enhances damage feature representation through the fusion of supervised and self-supervised signals, while improving inference efficiency and data utilization efficiency. The framework consists of the Focus-Diffusion Network (FDN) and Self-Contrastive Learning (SCL). FDN simulates the selective attention mechanism of the human visual system to enable dynamic sparse computation and feature diffusion, thereby improving inference efficiency. Meanwhile, lightweight difference perception and multi-scale interaction mechanisms are proposed to further enhance damage feature representation. And SCL avoids complex data augmentation and pretraining. It exploits semantic correlations within a single feature to construct contrastive samples for self-contrastive learning, thereby improving data utilization efficiency. Furthermore, this study constructs a high-resolution Gaza dataset with 35,939 damaged buildings. Experiments on the GE dataset (Global Earthquake dataset) and the Gaza dataset show that the F1 of FD-SC improves by at least 1.34% and 1.59%, respectively. And FD-SC contains only 3.34 M parameters and 4.25G FLOPs, achieving an inference speed of 39.92 FPS. Moreover, few-shot experiments confirm its robustness under data-scarce conditions, and transfer experiments on the Hawaii wildfire verify its strong generalization capability.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: CiviViL: multimodal interpretation of composite urban facility scenes with spatial-semantic-aware bidirectional cross-attention
record.abstract: Urban infrastructure and industrial facilities serve as the major carriers of urban lifeline systems, playing a pivotal role in enhancing urban resilience. These critical facilities are typically complexes composed of multiple components arranged in non-rigid layouts, characterized by form-function decoupling, limited data availability, and a lack of abundant crowd-sourced geospatial information. Existing approaches excel at backbone optimization for general scenes classification but fail to model the complex structural context and intricate relational dependencies essential for interpreting composite urban facility scenes. Though large vision-language models (VLMs) have revolutionized general scene understanding, their potential remains untapped in this domain due to the lack of specialized datasets and mechanisms for encoding domain-specific spatial semantics. To bridge this gap, we construct the first large-scale, fine-grained image-caption multimodal dataset for composite critical facility scenes, comprising 52,603 pairs, and then propose a structured representation method augmented by spatial-semantic decomposition, named CiviViL. Specifically, a vision foundation model is used to extract global image features, while a pre-trained transformer-based language model encodes multi-dimensional discrete spatial contexts associated with the configuration of functional components, including component distribution, facility-component relationships, and view-dependent spatial geometry. A bidirectional cross-attention mechanism (image-to-text and text-to-image) is designed to achieve collaborative reinforcement between visual perception and spatial-relational semantics, enabling the integration of complex associations into a unified scene representation. Extensive experimental results on 13 categories of infrastructure and industrial facilities demonstrate that CiviViL significantly outperforms 21 state-of-the-art baselines, underscoring the effectiveness and superiority of cross-modal collaborative enhancement for fine-grained interpretation of composite urban facility scenes.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: Modelling mountain pine beetle-impacted forest wildland fire fuel distributions from remotely piloted aircraft systems imagery and point clouds
record.abstract: This study compared 3D point cloud data derived from Structure-from-Motion (SfM) in 2021 and lidar in 2022 acquired using remotely piloted aircraft systems (RPAS). The overall objective was to develop and compare optical and active point cloud methods for deriving vegetation structures commonly measured in the field to quantify wildfire fuel distribution. The outcomes of the modelling framework were then applied to examine the impacts of mountain pine beetle (MPB) on canopy fuel load volumes in Jasper National Park prior to a high intensity wildfire in 2024. Tree species were classified using geographic object-based image analysis (GEOBIA) with an overall accuracy of ∼ 90%, with higher performance in relatively open canopies with minimal shadow. Photogrammetric and lidar point clouds resolved accurate individual tree height (R2 = 0.96; 0.99, respectively) when compared to field measurements. Crown base height derived using a windowed point density approach improved agreement with field data (R2 = 0.76; 0.91, respectively) and improved relative to previously reported methods. Across sites with varying MPB-induced tree mortality, plots dominated by dead conifers showed a redistribution of canopy fuels towards the ground compared to plots of mostly live conifers. This structural shift suggests increased ladder fuel development, reduced canopy continuity, and a heightened likelihood of surface to crown fire transition. The results demonstrate that RPAS point clouds can effectively characterize tree structure and improve crown base height estimation, supporting more accurate assessment of canopy bulk density. These measurements provide a viable alternative to labour-intensive field surveys and can then be used as calibration and validation data for broad-area forest assessment fuel modelling using airborne and satellite remotely sensed data.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: Fine-grained ship classification of remote sensing images based on class discrepancy learning network
record.abstract: Remote sensing imagery provides critical support for maritime situational awareness, vessel monitoring, and coastal management. Fine-grained classification of ships in such imagery aims to distinguish visually similar vessel types (e.g., cargo ships, oilers, and fishing boats), which is challenging due to intra-class variation caused by different sensors, observation angles, and complex backgrounds. To address this issue, we propose a class-discrepancy learning network (CDLNet) specifically designed for ship categories exhibiting imbalanced intra-class variation. An intra-class variation index is formulated to quantitatively assess category-specific diversity and guides a targeted adaptive learning strategy to enhance category-level discriminability. For classes with substantial appearance variations, a causally intervened masked attention module is introduced to adaptively capture diverse intra-class representations. The proposed method is particularly effective in remote sensing contexts, where diverse acquisition conditions significantly impact recognition performance. Extensive experiments conducted on two benchmark datasets for fine-grained ship classification in remote sensing imagery demonstrate the superior performance and generalization capability of the proposed method. On the FGSC-23 dataset, our method achieves 93.23% overall accuracy, surpassing the current state-of-the-art methods, including RGCRL-Net and other competitive baselines. The source code is available at https://github.com/MIPCLab/CDLNetcode.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: Towards individual agricultural parcel vectorization from VHR imagery: A coarse-to-fine and multi-task learning method
record.abstract: The vectorization of agricultural parcels is a foundational step in precision agriculture, enabling the monitoring of crop status and yield estimation. Existing methods struggle with two primary challenges: (1) overlapping parcels, caused by inaccurate localization in densely arranged fields, and (2) merged parcels, resulting from an inability to distinguish spectrally similar neighbors with narrow boundaries. We introduce IAPVec, a robust vectorization framework that leverages the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to address these limitations. Our approach integrates two key innovations: a coarse-to-fine prompt filter that refines region proposals to minimize overlaps, and a point-line ambiguous boundary enhancement module that explicitly guides the model to learn critical corner points and edge features. To support this research, we contribute the CAPCAD dataset—a large-scale, very high-resolution (0.5 m) benchmark with polygon annotations of 14,889 images, covering over 620 km2 of diverse agricultural parcel construction areas in China. Comparative experiments confirm that IAPVec sets a new state-of-the-art, outperforming existing methods by absolute gains of unless 1.8% in mask-focused metrics and 1.1% in boundary-focused metrics. This demonstrates its potential as a vital tool for advancing precision agricultural management and food security. The code is at https://github.com/ANAN200202/IAPVec.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: Robust detector-free multimodal image matching based on visual model guidance and gated attention
record.abstract: Multimodal image matching is a crucial foundational task for multi-source information fusion. However, severe geometric distortions and Non-linear Radiometric Differences (NRD) pose significant challenges to robust matching, such as the poor repeatability of keypoints. While detector-free methods emerge to mitigate this, current approaches relying on global context capture inadvertently aggregate irrelevant background noise, leading to reduced feature discriminability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a multimodal image matching method based on Visual Model Guidance and Gated Attention. First, we design a dual-stream backbone network that performs multi-scale fusion of high-level semantic priors from a visual foundation model with local geometric features from standard convolutions. This effectively enhances feature robustness against NRD and guides the model to focus on content-consistent regions. Second, to resolve the feature over-smoothing caused by global interactions, we propose a Gated Linear Attention (GLA) module. By employing a dynamic gating mechanism to filter out irrelevant global background noise, this module maximizes the preservation of local feature discriminability while incorporating effective long-range dependencies. Finally, we construct a coarse-to-fine multi-stage matching pipeline that cascades robust coarse matching with precise pixel-level refinement, achieving high-precision correspondence. Extensive experiments on four multimodal datasets (Optical-Infrared, Optical-SAR, Optical-Map, and Optical-Depth) demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly outperforming existing detector-based and detector-free baselines in terms of accuracy and robustness. The implementation of the proposed method will be made publicly available at https://github.com/yeyuanxin110/VMGGA.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: JointTrack: Densely joint feature extraction and interaction via temporal–spatial prompt learning for object tracking in multi-drone videos
record.abstract: Object tracking in multi-drone videos shows great potential in disaster emergency response, scene reconstruction and low-altitude economy due to its advantages of wide-area coverage and comprehensive perception. Most existing trackers adopt a decoupled framework, where each drone independently performs multi-stage feature extraction before multi-drone interaction. However, this paradigm suffers from inherent limitations, including task conflicts, mutual feature contamination and inconsistent target representations. To overcome above issues, this paper proposes JointTrack, a temporal–spatial prompt learning-based framework densely joints feature extraction and interaction in an end-to-end manner. Unlike prior methods, JointTrack incorporates multi-drone interaction at every feature extraction stage to achieve collaborative optimization. Specifically, a temporal prompt encoder (TPE) is proposed to capture temporal prompts from historical frames, guiding the network to disentangle target-related dynamics from background noise and thereby suppress feature contamination caused by occlusions or cluttered scenes. Meanwhile, a spatial prompt encoder (SPE) constructs scale-aware and component-aware prompts by integrating multi-drone templates, enabling feature complementarity that alleviate inconsistent feature representations under varying viewpoints. Additionally, a dynamic gated decoder (DGD) adaptively fuse these temporal–spatial prompts into original features through a gating mechanism with contextual dependency modeling. Extensive experiments on the MDOT benchmark demonstrate that JointTrack outperforms previous state-of-the-art trackers by 4.1% and 3.0% in success and precision. Moreover, JointTrack maintains competitive tracking speed and exhibits strong generalizability on the MDMT and UAV123 datasets, as well as in real-world scenarios. Codes will be released at https://github.com/HanJin0326/JointTrack.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: Towards generalized spaceborne SAR ship detection via Fourier-based perturbation augmentation and quality-aware invariance learning
record.abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) ship detection is essential for maritime situational awareness. As spaceborne SAR platforms continue to expand, there is an urgent demand for detectors that can generalize to new or unseen platforms. However, existing methods are typically tailored to specific platforms and suffer significant performance degradation on unseen data due to inherent distribution shifts and limited generalization ability. To alleviate this, we propose a generalized SAR ship detection framework through Fourier-based perturbation Augmentation and Quality-Aware invariance learning, termed FAQA. FAQA aims to integrate multiple platform SAR data to learn generalized ship representations, boosting detection on previously unseen data. Specifically, to improve the model’s adaptability to unknown data, a Fourier-based Perturbation Augmentation (FPA) strategy is proposed. FPA simulates potential unknown domains by applying controlled random perturbations to the low-frequency amplitude regions, while preserving semantic integrity. Then, a Quality-Aware Invariance Learning method (QAIL) is developed. QAIL jointly evaluates the location-classification quality of each proposal as guidance, prompting the model to focus on invariance learning of semantically reliable ship regions while suppressing SAR-specific background interference. Lastly, an Adaptive Parameter Search (APS) mechanism is designed. APS leverages gradient alignment between original and augmented images as the supervisory signal, adaptively steering optimization toward more generalized solutions. Experimental results show that FAQA consistently outperforms existing DG methods across diverse settings. Under multi-DG, it achieves an average AP gain of 2.24% across four target domains. Under single-DG, it achieves gains of 2.35%, 0.59%, and 3.37% across three cases, demonstrating superior generalization and robustness to domain shifts.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: Motion consistency-guided spatiotemporal learning: a robust framework for low-altitude infrared object detection
record.abstract: Low-altitude infrared object detection is a fundamental technology for airspace surveillance and wide-area monitoring. However, accurately detecting dim and tiny targets remains highly challenging in complex scenes, where targets are often captured under low signal-to-noise ratio conditions and appear as weak responses embedded in drifting clouds, swaying vegetation, and other background clutter. Although multi-frame methods can exploit temporal information to enhance target perception, distinguishing target-related motion from clutter-induced motion remains difficult when both targets and dynamic background vary across frames. To address this challenge, we propose a Motion Consistency-Guided Fusion Network (MCFNet) for low-altitude infrared object detection. Specifically, we first develop a bio-inspired motion perception mechanism that combines ON/OFF pathway modeling with fractional-order temporal integration to improve sensitivity to weak motion. Building on this, we further design a motion consistency encoding strategy that estimates motion intensity and adaptively adjusts directional offsets to alleviate motion-scale mismatch while capturing motion directionality and trajectory coherence. These encoded motion cues are then introduced into an adaptive fusion process through a consistency-aware cross-attention mechanism, which retrieves and reinforces target-relevant spatial features while suppressing contamination caused by background-induced pseudo-motion. Comprehensive experiments on the Anti-UAV410, ITSDT-15 K, and IRDST benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive performance, reaching an AP50 of 82.59% on the dynamic Anti-UAV410 dataset and improving AP50 by 11.43% on IRDST. Moreover, the model shows favorable robustness in complex environments characterized by intense clutter and scale variations. The source code is available at https://github.com/SZUUI/MCFNet.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: Fine-grained heterogeneous change detection in complex disaster response with wavelet-based spatial-frequency coupled learning
record.abstract: Heterogeneous remote sensing change detection (CD) based on optical and SAR imagery is essential for rapid disaster monitoring, as it overcomes single-sensor limitations and enables all-weather observation. However, the inherent heterogeneity between optical and SAR modalities—stemming from their disparate imaging mechanisms—results in poor feature comparability, significantly impeding fine-grained, accurate change identification. To address the issue, this study explores a combination of data-level strategies and methodological enhancements. First, to alleviate the data scarcity, this study constructs two sub-meter (0.35 m) heterogeneous datasets tailored for earthquake building damage and flood assessment, thereby providing a high-resolution data foundation for fine-grained disaster monitoring. Second, a Siamese Spatial–Frequency Coupled Network (SSFCNet) is introduced to mitigate the cross-modal discrepancy. Specifically, a Spatial-Frequency Coupled Encoder (SFCE) is designed to simultaneously model spatial semantics and frequency directional features via wavelet transforms, thereby aligning heterogeneous representations while mitigating noise. To refine change representation, an Explicit Change Guidance Module (ECGM) is designed to incorporate distinct difference priors into the decoding stage. Subsequently, a Multi-scale Inverse Wavelet Decoder (MIWD) exploits the invertibility of wavelet transforms to restore high-frequency details, preventing information loss during upsampling. Finally, a Boundary-Aware Loss (BAL) is devised to enforce geometric consistency along change boundaries through gradient constraints. Extensive experiments on five public datasets and the two newly constructed datasets demonstrate that SSFCNet significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of detection accuracy and boundary integrity. Notably, the proposed method achieves an optimal balance between performance and computational efficiency, demonstrating its potential for rapid, robust emergency response. For reproducibility, our code and data are available at https://github.com/yangyang12318/SSFCNet.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: FreqChange: Frequency-aware spatiotemporal learning with prior guidance for semantic change detection in remote sensing images
record.abstract: Semantic change detection plays a critical role in monitoring Earth’s surface dynamics by identifying the locations and semantic categories of changes from bi-temporal remote sensing images. Existing methods primarily employ a shared-weight image encoder coupled with a change extractor to detect changes in the spatial domain, while lacking sufficient temporal modeling and effective exploitation of semantic priors. As a result, they struggle to accurately localize changed regions and maintain intra-class semantic consistency. To address these limitations, we propose FreqChange, a frequency-aware spatiotemporal learning framework with semantic prior guidance. Specifically, a frequency change-aware module (FCAM) is integrated into the spatiotemporal learning framework to accurately perceive and localize changed regions by comprehensively analyzing both low- and high-frequency components between bi-temporal features. Additionally, to enhance the intra-class semantic consistency of bi-temporal images, we propose a semantic consistency enhancement module (SCEM), which leverages semantic priors derived from large-scale pre-trained vision foundation models, combined with semantic consistency upsampling, to effectively facilitate spatiotemporal learning. Through their collaborative integration, these modules collectively enable the precise detection of land cover changes from bi-temporal images while preserving intra-class semantic consistency. Extensive experiments on four well-recognized datasets (i.e., HRSCD, SECOND, HiUCD-mini, and Landsat-SCD) demonstrate that FreqChange consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative metrics and qualitative visualizations. By uniting frequency-domain analysis and semantic priors, FreqChange establishes a new paradigm for accurate and reliable semantic change detection in remote sensing.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: MiMNet-STASF: a spatiotemporal decoupled network for sub-pixel canopy structure retrieval of urban forests with multi-source long-term remote sensing time series
record.abstract: Forest canopy height (FCH) and vertical structural composition are essential for urban ecological assessment and precision forest management, yet reliable retrieval in fragmented urban–rural transition landscapes remains challenging due to multi-source sensor heterogeneity, seasonal dynamics, and mixed canopy conditions within 10 m pixels. We propose MiMNet-STASF, a spatiotemporal fusion framework for grid-level canopy-structure inversion from 24-month Sentinel-1/2 time series. The framework integrates a nested Mamba architecture (Inner VMamba for multi-scale spatial encoding and Outer bidirectional Mamba for long-range temporal dependency modeling), an adaptive Spatiotemporal Arbiter Gated Fusion (STASF) module (SG/TG/STAG), and a physics-informed hierarchical regression head that jointly estimates FCH and vertical structural fractions (<10 m, 10–20 m, and ≥20 m). Using UAV LiDAR-derived supervision, validated in Xiong’an New Area against 13 deep learning models spanning four architectural paradigms (RNNs, CNNs, Transformers, SSMs), MiMNet-STASF outperforms all comparatives, achieving an R2 of 0.8963 and an RMSE of 1.0903 m for FCH retrieval. Ablation results indicate that the nested Mamba and STASF components provide clearer gains on structurally imbalanced targets. From a data perspective, Sentinel-1 provides enhanced structural sensitivity, Sentinel-2 offers stable spectral and phenological context, and vegetation indices (VI) further improve vegetation contrast; their fusion enhances prediction consistency across canopy-height gradients and vertical fractional components. Moreover, MiMNet-STASF retains robust structural representations under seasonal vegetation variation. Together with cross-regional GEDI-referenced evaluation, these results support MiMNet-STASF as an effective and scalable solution for management-oriented, fine-grained urban forest canopy-structure mapping. The implementation of the proposed method is publicly available at https://github.com/qinjs123/MiMNet-STASF.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: All-in-one texture restoration of building Façade with generative diffusion prior
record.abstract: The texture mapping of building façades in 3D real scene reconstruction often suffers from distortion, occlusion, color discrepancy and missing region, resulting in low-quality (LQ) and degraded visual fidelity. Existing methods mainly address only a single type of defect or are tailored to specific scenarios, limiting their ability to restore high-quality (HQ) textures in complex real-world settings. In this work, we propose an all-in-one building façade texture restoration framework that comprehensively simulates and restores diverse texture defects. Firstly, we design a practical façade degradation model that simulates real-world defects and enables network training solely on synthetic data, effectively addressing the challenge of acquiring paired HQ-LQ datasets. Moreover, we develop a restoration network based on Stable Diffusion (SD), which serves as a powerful natural image prior, incorporating a multimodal prompt strategy that combines textual prompts and defect probability map prompts to provide both global semantic and local defect-specific guidance. To further improve the network’s capability in handling and restoring complex defects, we design a dual-path feature guidance strategy, which leverages condition information from ControlNet and multi-scale defect features extracted from the defect probability map to enable staged control over the denoising process, facilitating accurate geometric alignment and detailed texture restoration. To support comprehensive evaluation in real-world scenarios, we construct a real façade defect dataset, providing a reliable benchmark for façade texture restoration. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework shows superior restoration quality and generalization capability, especially in real-world scenarios and out-of-distribution conditions. The code and dataset will be available at: https://github.com/xaliu116/DiffFTR.

record.title: DCMArb: Decoupled-Collaborative Mamba for Arbitrary-scale Hyperspectral Super-resolution
record.abstract: Hyperspectral imagery (HSI) super-resolution (SR) aims to recover high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs. However, existing methods typically apply homogeneous processing to spatial-spectral features, leading to heterogeneity conflicts at the physical level. Specifically, the spatial dimension primarily exhibits locally continuous long-range dependencies, while the spectral dimension presents non-stationary and non-linear irregular coupling characteristics driven by the physical responses of ground objects. Such homogeneous feature extraction approaches lead to mutual interference between spatial structures and spectral correlations during modeling. This, in turn, results in limitations such as spatial blur and spectral drift in the reconstructed outcomes, as well as insufficient generalization and adaptability in continuous scale mapping. To alleviate the aforementioned challenges, this paper proposes an arbitrary-scale SR network named DCMArb (Decoupled-Collaborative Mamba for Arbitrary-scale Super-resolution), based on a decoupled-collaborative-reconstruction paradigm. In specific implementation, this method tightly integrates physical mechanism analysis with network module design. First, the multi-dimensional dependency extraction stage (MDES) is proposed as the decoupling unit. It separates spatial long-range dependencies and spectral non-linear correlations through differentiated modeling to avoid the mutual interference between heterogeneous features, establishing a pure feature representation foundation. Next, the heterogeneous feature integration stage (HFIS) is designed as the collaborative unit. It introduces an adaptive mechanism to dynamically balance the decoupled pure features and filtered key details, thereby constructing a high-quality, interference-resistant spatial-spectral joint prior. Finally, the scale-aware meta-learned upsampler block (SMUB) is constructed as the reconstruction unit. Utilizing a mixture-of-experts mechanism, it maps this high-quality prior to a manifold function in the continuous scale space and performs high-fidelity arbitrary-scale (including non-integer) continuous reconstruction, thereby mitigating distortion issues in cross-scale transformations. Extensive experiments on three benchmarks demonstrate that DCMArb achieves competitive or superior performance compared with state-of-the-art single-scale and arbitrary-scale methods in both quantitative metrics and visual quality. Ablation studies and complexity analyses further validate that the proposed framework achieves superior performance and generalization with reduced computational costs. The source code will be made available at https://github.com/wangswhu/DCMArb.

record.title: WaveUNet: An efficient deep network based on discrete wavelet transform and attention mechanism for InSAR phase unwrapping
record.abstract: Phase unwrapping (PU) is a core yet challenging step in interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) measurements. Traditional PU methods rely on the assumption of phase continuity, which often fails in areas with steep topography, dense fringes, or severe decorrelation noise. While deep learning has emerged to address this limitation, existing networks suffer from two key drawbacks: (1) limited generalization due to training data that inadequately captures the complexity of real-world deformation, and (2) high computational costs caused by the use of deep architectures with extensive parameters and high-dimensional convolutions to pursue accuracy. These two factors lead to the insufficient generalization capability and considerable consumption of computing resources for these networks. To address these issues, this study presents a lightweight deep phase unwrapping network based on the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and attention mechanism, called WaveUNet. To train this network, we first simulate InSAR phase data to generate a sample dataset encompassing complex topographic and deformation features; subsequently, WaveUNet is trained by integrating the DWT and attention mechanism, achieving phase unwrapping with high precision and less computational resources; finally, we conduct tests on WaveUNet using the simulated dataset, the InSAR-DLPU dataset, and real InSAR data. The experimental results demonstrate that the GPU usage of WaveUNet is 32.96%, 24.43%, and 38.63% of that for VURNet, ResUNet, and PUNet, respectively. Meanwhile, its total number of floating-point operations (FLOPs) is merely 21.80%, 23.81%, and 9.23% of that for the three models, respectively. This illustrates that WaveUNet achieves comparable accuracy and efficiency to state-of-the-art PU models while utilizing limited computational resources. The related experimental code will be made available at https://github.com/xiangHQ/WaveUNet.git.

record.title: BIM-vSLAM: Bridging BIM and visual SLAM with plane-based representation for automated registration and image-based reconstruction
record.abstract: Robust localization in cluttered indoor environments is essential for embodied Artificial Intelligence (AI). Traditional localization systems rely on expert-generated maps, which increases costs and limits adaptability to dynamic settings. Building Information Models (BIMs) are commonly recognized formats that represent fixed architectural elements. However, integrating BIM with Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) remains challenging due to divergent data structures. BIM encodes environments as semantically rich planar objects, whereas SLAM constructs maps from sparse, localized feature clusters that capture fine-grained details but lack explicit planar context. This representational gap hinders robust correspondence and risks misalignment in complex indoor scenes. This paper proposes a lightweight visual SLAM system that bridges this gap using planes as a unifying representation. We transform BIM into a hierarchical, topometric semantic map with planar features delineating rooms and corridors. Simultaneously, we reformulate the SLAM map as a lightweight geometric model of horizontal and vertical planes, replacing conventional occupancy grids or point clouds. This plane-based representation leverages scene structure to reduce computational complexity while maximizing estimation accuracy. The representation is tightly integrated into the SLAM system, enabling precise short-term tracking and mapping between keyframes, and facilitating global alignment with persistent BIM architectural features (e.g., walls and doors) to mitigate drift. Both local and global components are unified within a graph optimization framework. Experiments on challenging indoor benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art accuracy and efficiency. The system achieves higher global BIM registration recall rate with 3 times faster than SOTA image-based methods and point-cloud registration, it further reduces Absolute Pose Error by 90% and delivers faster map reconstruction with significantly lower storage. Source code is available at https://github.com/csongae/BIM-vSLAM.

record.title: PRGD: Proximal Residual-Guided Diffusion with pattern-aware experts for remote sensing image super-resolution
record.abstract: High-resolution remote sensing imagery is essential for accurate Earth observation and analysis. While diffusion models show promise for image super-resolution (SR), their application to remote sensing is often hindered by fidelity loss from error accumulation and by inadequate guidance from simple low-resolution (LR) conditioning. To address these dual challenges, we introduce the Proximal Residual-Guided Diffusion (PRGD) model, a novel framework for high-fidelity remote sensing SR. PRGD is built upon a novel holistic paradigm designed to synergistically mitigate error accumulation throughout the diffusion process. This paradigm combines a Residual Shifting strategy, which simplifies the generation path by anchoring it to the LR image, with a measurement-consistent Proximal Sampling technique that enforces strict data fidelity at each iterative step. To provide superior guidance, PRGD introduces an innovative Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) feature extraction module, powered by our Pattern-Aware Deformable Convolution (PADC). This novel convolution dynamically groups feature channels based on their activation patterns to extract rich, adaptive, multi-scale priors. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that PRGD achieves a new state-of-the-art, establishing superior performance across both fidelity and perceptual quality. For instance, on the Toronto ×4 dataset, PRGD not only surpasses the leading regression-based method in PSNR but also reduces the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) by 11.96% compared to the next-best diffusion model. The resulting images exhibit superior fidelity to the ground truth, enhanced visual realism, and remarkable detail preservation, thereby enhancing the potential of diffusion models to serve as a reliable data source for downstream remote sensing applications.

record.title: CDHNet: An implicit calibration and difference-guided hierarchical perception change detection network for remote sensing images
record.abstract: Deep learning has become a common approach for constructing change detection models that help extract semantic features from raw remote sensing images. However, relying solely on semantic information derived from imprecisely aligned images can lead to the entanglement of change-relevant and irrelevant observations, restricting the representation of differences between images and resulting in pseudo‑changes. To address these issues, this study proposes an implicit calibration and difference-guided hierarchical perception network (CDHNet), which integrates spatiotemporal consistency modeling with difference representation learning to enhance the discriminability of change features. Unlike conventional feature extraction strategies, CDHNet introduces an implicit calibration and difference-guided augmentation (CDA) module that enhances spatial correspondence between bi-temporal images and labels through pixel-level self-calibration and further reinforces spatiotemporal consistency via inter-branch mutual alignment. Building on this calibration, multi-order feature differences are extracted to mitigate the degradation of change-relevant representations caused by the locality of convolutional operations. Furthermore, CDHNet designs a staged dual-domain interaction (SDI) module, which enables cross-attentional integration between calibrated semantic and hierarchical difference features, thereby achieving a balanced representation of background and changes while enhancing the diversity of feature extraction. In the decoder, an adaptive multi-scale perception (AMP) module is designed to progressively improve discriminative perception along both channel and spatial dimensions, maintaining spatial coherence to achieve multi-scale object discrimination and enable accurate identification of both local changes and structural transitions. Experiments on four public and two unregistered datasets demonstrate that CDHNet outperforms the benchmark methods, particularly in preserving spatial completeness under complex global variations and accurately identifying subtle regional changes. The code for this work will be available on GitHub.

record.title: TALineNet: A benchmark and network for temporally-aware continuous line segment detection in event streams
record.abstract: Event cameras offer unique advantages for line segment detection in high-speed and high-dynamic-range scenarios, yet existing methods face two critical limitations. They primarily operate on isolated event frames, overlooking temporal continuity and unstable imaging within continuous streams. Furthermore, the lack of absolute intensity renders these methods highly susceptible to noise, hindering reliable spatial feature extraction. To bridge this gap, we first establish two novel benchmarks, Ev-WireframeSeq (synthetic) and Ev-LineSeq (real-world), providing the first sequential event-based line segment detection datasets with dense line annotations to facilitate temporal context learning. Supported by these benchmarks, we propose TALineNet, a temporally-aware network that delivers temporally consistent and spatially robust line segment detection from continuous event streams. The network leverages a recurrent backbone to capture long-range temporal dependencies and employs a background-line disentanglement (BLD) module to suppress noise and emphasize true edge structures. Moreover, a Bézier-based representation is adopted in the detection head to better accommodate the non-uniform spatial distributions in event data. To quantitatively assess detection stability over time, we introduce a set of sequence-level evaluation metrics, including the Geometric Stability Score (GSS) and Temporal Fidelity Index (TFI). Experimental results demonstrate that TALineNet achieves 57.7% msAP on the Ev-LineSeq dataset, outperforming the state-of-the-art by 12.9 percentage points. The source code and datasets are available at https://github.com/Qiuben/TALineNet.

record.title: HCFNet: Hierarchical and complementary feature embedding for remote sensing change captioning
record.abstract: Remote sensing change captioning (RS-CC) aims to describe changes between bi-temporal remote sensing images in natural language. Existing methods commonly encode visual changes into a single fused difference feature, which may limit the utilization of change information with different extents during caption generation. In addition, conventional n-gram-based metrics are insensitive to mismatches in spatial scale and change extent. To address these issues, a Hierarchical and Complementary Feature Embedding Network (HCFNet) is proposed. Specifically, the Change-Cognitive Visual Parser (CCVP) extracts branch-specific change embeddings from the fused difference feature through parallel aggregation with different spatial preferences. Hierarchical Cognition Mining Loss (HCMLoss) utilizes the change intensity derived from the change mask to form the Hierarchical Cognitive Vector (HCoV). The Change-Cognitive Language Decoder (CCLD) further incorporates branch-specific HCoV into different decoding layers through multi-stage feature fusion. In addition, the Change-Sensitive Metric (CSM) complements traditional n-gram-based metrics with a change-scene penalty term, thereby improving sensitivity to spatial-scale and change-extent mismatches. Experiments are conducted on three benchmark datasets, LEVIR-CC, WHU-CDC, and SECOND-CC. The results demonstrate that the proposed HCFNet achieves competitive performance, validating the effectiveness of HCoV in remote sensing change captioning. The implementation code and vocabulary of CSM will be publicly available at https://github.com/Hope21maker/HCFNet.

record.title: A vertical FVC profile retrieval method (OLV-FVC) based on airborne LiDAR point cloud under the constraint of optical remote sensing for forest plots
record.abstract: The vertical fractional vegetation cover (FVC) profile is a critical metric for quantifying the three-dimensional (3D) structural heterogeneity and ecological functions of forest ecosystems. Current LiDAR-based FVC estimation techniques face several constraints, including substantial dependence on point cloud classification, insufficient representation of understory vegetation structures, and difficulty in retrieving the herbaceous layer FVC. This study proposes a physically grounded approach: the Optical remote sensing-constrained LiDAR Vertical FVC profile retrieval method for forest plots (OLV-FVC). The methodological novelty of OLV-FVC lies in its non-classification-dependent stratified point cloud reconstruction, its compensation for underestimated understory coverage, and its physically interpretable quantitative conversion from 2D planar FVC to 3D stratified FVC. Specifically, OLV-FVC reconstructs the uppermost point cloud structure of each vegetation layer by leveraging spatial occlusion modeling and multi-echo pairing, thereby reducing reliance on traditional point cloud classification. A spectral–structural coupled correction mechanism is then developed to mitigate LiDAR signal omission in occluded understory regions and compensate for the underestimation of shrub- and herbaceous-layer coverage. Finally, based on geometric optical models and gap probability theory, OLV-FVC establishes a physically interpretable framework to quantitatively convert 2D planar FVC into 3D stratified FVC, enabling the independent estimation of canopy, shrub, and herbaceous layers. The efficacy of OLV-FVC was rigorously evaluated through a hierarchical validation scheme involving theoretical modeling, radiative transfer simulations (LESS), and multi-temporal field observations. The understory correction mechanism substantially improved the estimation accuracy, reducing the average RMSE by 0.066 and 0.078 and increasing the mean R2 by 0.016 and 0.106 for the shrub and herbaceous layers, respectively. Across all validation phases, OLV-FVC exhibited robust performance, achieving high consistency in theoretical assessments and simulation experiments (R2: 0.807–0.998; RMSE: 0.009–0.113) and proving its practical utility across distinct forest types and phenological stages (R2: 0.794–0.990; RMSE: 0.019–0.122). Sensitivity analyses further confirmed that OLV-FVC maintains high stability across varying point cloud densities and terrain slopes. Overall, OLV-FVC provides a robust and physically interpretable approach for stratified FVC estimation, offering significant potential for fine-scale forest monitoring and ecological modeling. The field datasets used in this study are publicly available through the National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON) Data Portal (https://data.neonscience.org/), and the source code for OLV-FVC is available at https://github.com/zhangh-geo/OLV-FVC.

record.title: Fusion of hyperspectral and multisource remote sensing data using intelligent optimized ensemble learning to estimate the SOC content of seven mangrove species in China
record.abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) in mangrove ecosystems represents a vital blue carbon resource; however, accurate characterization of its spatial heterogeneity remains challenging. Traditional approaches treat mangroves as homogeneous entities, which overlooks variations in carbon sequestration capacity among species and severely limits precise assessments of carbon sink functionality. To address this issue, this study pioneers the integration of multiple intelligent optimization algorithms with an ensemble learning regression model (PSO-ELR), fusing hyperspectral data simulated by the PROSPECT-PRO and 4-SCALE models with multisource satellite data (Gao Fen (GF), Sentinel-2 (S2), and Sentinel-1 (S1)), providing an indirect physical link between canopy remote sensing data and subsurface SOC, thereby enabling high-precision estimates of SOC content for seven typical mangrove species in China. The study revealed that different mangrove species exhibit unique spectral responses at the leaf scale, with the red edge, near-infrared, and shortwave infrared bands being the most sensitive for estimating SOC. Additionally, compared with genetic algorithm optimization (GAO) and the grid search method (GSM), the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm significantly outperforms the other algorithms. The PSO-ELR model exhibits the highest SOC estimation accuracy (R2 = 0.873–0.925) across the various datasets and demonstrated robust generalizability. Finally, the results of this study confirmed that mangrove species identity is the primary driver of spatial variation in SOC, with Bruguiera gymnorrhiza (BG) and Aegiceras corniculatum (AC) being the mangrove species with the highest carbon density (301.46 and 300.29 Mg/ha, respectively). This study recommends prioritizing the conservation and planting of existing high-carbon-density species (BG and AC) and optimizing the maintenance of widespread pioneer species such as Avicennia marina (AM) and Kandelia candel (KC) to achieve precise protection of mangrove ecosystems and maximize carbon sink benefits in restoration practices.

record.title: SMS-Diff: Physics-aware spectral-spatial diffusion for unified geospatial multi-modal reconstruction
record.abstract: In recent years, unified generative models have achieved unprecedented success in photorealistic synthesis. However, since satellite imagery serves as strict physical measurements, the geospatial domain requires capturing the complex multi-modal symbiosis across diverse sensors to achieve rigorous structural and spectral fidelity rather than mere visual realism. Currently, constrained by multi-modal data scarcity and inherent modality barriers, existing studies often fail to reconstruct underlying physical interactions and remain restricted to superficial perceptual synthesis. To address these challenges, we present the MMG-5 dataset and the unified SMS-Diff model. MMG-5 is a globally sampled, strictly aligned benchmark integrating five geospatial modalities (LULC, RGB, SWIR, SAR, DEM) to bridge the multi-modal data gap. Building on MMG-5, SMS-Diff transforms geospatial image translation into true multi-modal physics-aware reconstruction. Specifically, SMS-Diff incorporates a Spectral Manifold Injector (SMI) and a Latent Physics Resonance Loss (LPRL) to explicitly decouple spectral laws from spatial geometry, successfully bridging global frequency alignment and local structural precision. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SMS-Diff achieves consistent improvements over strong baselines, achieving an SSIM of 0.315 and LPIPS of 0.307. Beyond generic computer vision metrics, we integrate classic geospatial physical indicators with downstream task utility as the dual benchmark for validating geospatial consistency. Crucially, these task-specific evaluations reveal a significant “Denoising Effect Tendency” in synthesized features, yielding partial accuracy inversions over raw sensor data. The model shows zero-shot transfer ability for change detection to some extent, while also scaling to reconstruction across 10 diverse modalities and multiple downstream tasks via low-resource fine-tuning. In summary, SMS-Diff drives a paradigm shift toward internally consistent physics-aware reconstruction, proving the feasibility of generative models to simulate the real physical world.

record.title: MRIo3DS-Net: a mutually reinforcing images to 3D surface RNN-like framework for model-adaptation indoor 3D reconstruction
record.abstract: Currently, deep neural networks (DNNs) have made some progresses in local region feature extraction, image matching under difficult conditions and point cloud surface optimization in photogrammetry and computer vision. However, there have been being no reports on an end-to-end high-accuracy 3D reconstruction network that integrated point cloud generation (i.e., dense image matching) and 3D surface optimization. Moreover, deep-learning-based 3D reconstruction networks are often difficult to apply to new dataset tasks. Therefore, this paper is the first to propose an end-to-end framework of mutually reinforcing images to 3D surface recurrent neural network (RNN)-like (MRIo3DS-Net) for model-adaptation indoor 3D reconstruction, where multi-view dense matching and point cloud surface optimization are mutually reinforced by a RNN-like structure rather than being treated as a separate issue. The characteristics and advantages of this framework are as follows: (1) In the multi-view dense matching module (MVDMM), the model-adaptation strategy is used to fine-tune and optimize a Transformer-based multi-view dense matching DNN, so that it has the higher image feature for matching and detail expression capabilities; (2) In the point cloud surface optimization module (PCSOM), the 3D surface reconstruction network based on 3D implicit field is optimized by using model-adaptation strategy, which solves the problem of point cloud surface optimization without knowing normal vector of 3D surface. Especially, to improve and finely reconstruct 3D surfaces from point cloud, smooth loss function with an edge-preserving strategy is proposed and added to this module; (3) The proposed MRIo3DS-Net is a RNN-like framework, which utilizes the finely optimized 3D surface obtained by PCSOM to recursively reinforce the differentiable warping for optimizing MVDMM. This refinement leads to achieving better dense matching results, and better dense matching results leads to achieving better 3D surface results recursively and mutually. Hence, model-adaptation strategy can better collaborate the differences between the two network modules, so that they complement each other to achieve the better effect; (4) To accelerate the transfer learning and training convergence from source domain to target domain, a multi-task loss function based on Bayesian uncertainty is used to adaptively adjust the weights between the two networks loss functions of MVDMM and PCSOM; (5) In this multi-task cascade network framework, theoretically, the two aforementioned modules possess the inherent potential to be replaced by arbitrary corresponding state-of-the-art (SOTA) networks to achieve better 3D reconstruction results. We tested performance of MRIo3DS-Net in the DTU, Tanks and Temples datasets by comparison experiments and ablation experiments with SOTA networks. The results show that MRIo3DS-Net has achieved the best performance and can reconstruct various indoor scenes reliably, completely and accurately. MRIo3DS-Net can provide a new end-to-end framework for high-accuracy indoor 3D reconstruction and has certain potential for the new target domain task.

record.title: Segmentation-guided and attention-enhanced GAN for SAR image restoration under multi-type interference
record.abstract: Spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems are often affected by co-frequency interference, which significantly degrades imaging quality and subsequent image interpretation performance. Existing suppression methods typically focus on a single interference type or salient interference, which limits their effectiveness when confronted with multi-type real-measured interference. To address these challenges, this paper reformulates the multi-type interference suppression problem as a pre-imaging clean SAR echo restoration task, and proposes a novel SC2-GAN framework for SAR imaging. Built upon a generative adversarial network, SC2-GAN integrates three synergistic components: segmentation-guided mechanism (SGM), convolutional block attention module (CBAM), and conditionally parameterized convolution module (CondConv). The SGM extracts the spatial location and type information of interference in shallow feature space, enabling differentiated attention to multiple interference types. CBAM captures discriminative features in both channel and spatial through dual attention mechanisms, enhancing the network’s ability to perceive interference features in deeper layers. CondConv adaptively generates convolutional kernels according to input features, enabling the network to respond differently to diverse interference intensities and patterns in the parameter space. The synergy of these components forms the foundation of SC2-GAN’s adaptability to multi-type and multi-intensity interference. In addition, SC2-GAN achieves accurate interference suppression and segmentation in an end-to-end manner using a shared network architecture. Experiments conducted on seven simulated datasets and ten real-measured Sentinel-1 datasets demonstrate that the proposed SC2-GAN can suppress multiple types of interference and improved SAR imaging quality. The source code and datasets are publicly available at: https://github.com/XIAOYU-XU2805/SC2-GAN.

record.title: Foggy-UAVCD and DSRF-Net: Benchmarking robust satellite–UAV change detection under fog degradation
record.abstract: Synergistic observation using multimodal remote sensing data is crucial for rapid geographic monitoring. However, acquiring large-scale multimodal datasets remains a significant challenge. While Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) is often used for all-weather monitoring, its inherent speckle noise and limited semantic interpretability constrain its application in fine-grained change detection (CD). In contrast, Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery offers superior spatial resolution and flexible deployment, yet its optical sensors are highly susceptible to adverse weather. In practical emergency response, fog degradation frequently introduces severe visibility reduction and pseudo-changes, creating a gap between ideal laboratory settings and real-world deployment. To address these challenges, we first construct Foggy-UAVCD, a novel heterogeneous benchmark specifically designed for SAT–UAV CD under foggy conditions. By simulating controllable fog-induced visibility degradation, this dataset serves as a specialized benchmark for evaluating cross-modal geometric alignment and robust feature extraction. Furthermore, we propose the Dual-Stage Rectification and Fusion Network (DSRF-Net), a lightweight yet robust architecture. Specifically, a Cross-modal Feature Rectification (CFR) module is designed to suppress fog-induced noise by leveraging satellite priors, while a Dual-Domain Fusion Upsampler (DDFU) module is developed to recover high-frequency boundary details. Experimental results on the Foggy-UAVCD and HTCD datasets demonstrate that DSRF-Net achieves a competitive trade-off between accuracy and efficiency, with only 3.43M parameters and 1.84G floating point operations (FLOPs), indicating potential for efficient adverse-weather remote sensing analysis, while further validation across broader geographic regions, climate zones, and seasonal conditions is still required. Code and dataset will be available at https://github.com/xiaobing-min/DSRFNet.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: PELNet: A general physics-embedded learning framework for polarimetric target decomposition
record.abstract: Polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) provides full polarimetric measurements, from which physically meaningful scattering parameters can be derived through target decomposition. Traditional model-driven methods often suffer from rigid power allocation, sensitivity to noise, and limited capability in representing complex scattering scenes. In contrast, deep learning-based approaches can learn intricate scattering patterns directly from data with greater flexibility. Nevertheless, these purely data-driven methods usually model scattering mechanisms as black boxes, resulting in limited physical interpretability and reduced generalization to complex or unseen scenarios. Building on these observations, we investigate the integration of physical priors into deep neural networks and propose PELNet, a physics-embedded end-to-end framework for polarimetric target decomposition. The core innovation of PELNet lies in structurally embedding a differentiable scattering model within the network decoder, establishing a strict correspondence between the latent space and interpretable physical parameters. Specifically, a multi-scale SE-attention encoder is used to extract context-aware polarimetric features, while a lightweight Mixture-of-Experts module enables adaptive modeling of different volume scattering components. Furthermore, a differentiable scattering reconstruction layer embeds the physical scattering model directly into the network decoder, establishing an interpretable mapping between latent representations and physical parameters. A physically guided loss function is further introduced to enhance reconstruction fidelity and spatial consistency. Experiments on multi-band PolSAR datasets across diverse terrain types demonstrate that PELNet achieves superior accuracy and interpretability compared to traditional methods, providing a new perspective for PolSAR image interpretation and physical parameter inversion. The source code and pretrained models are publicly available at https://github.com/shurongz/PhyDecomp.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: SAF-CropNet: Spatially adaptive fusion of SAR and optical imagery for semantic segmentation in operational cropland mapping across regions
record.abstract: Accurate cropland mapping from remote sensing imagery is essential for agricultural monitoring, food security assessment, and land resource management. Although optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) observations provide complementary information for cropland extraction, their local contributions vary across imaging conditions, land-cover backgrounds, parcel morphologies, and regional agricultural systems. This variability limits direct concatenation and static fusion, as modality-specific errors may propagate into segmentation outputs in the absence of spatially adaptive weighting. This study proposes SAF-CropNet, a spatially adaptive SAR–optical fusion framework for binary cropland semantic segmentation. Specifically, SAF-CropNet first extracts modality-specific SAR structural features and optical spectral-textural features through separate encoder branches. The Paired Reciprocal Inter-modal Selective Modulator enhances complementary SAR–optical interactions, while the Contextual State-space Modeling module captures long-range parcel organization. A spatially adaptive fusion head then estimates per-pixel contribution weights for SAR, optical, and contextual features before decoding. Evaluation was conducted on a seven-area SAR–optical benchmark spanning China, Germany, and France. The benchmark integrates GF1/GF3 and Sentinel-1/2 imagery with reference labels derived from field surveys and RapidCrops products and covers fragmented smallholder systems, water-rich and peri-urban mosaics, and large mechanized cropland. Within-region five-fold validation shows that SAF-CropNet achieves an average F1 score of 0.8550 and an mIoU of 0.8068, outperforming the evaluated segmentation baselines while remaining lightweight, with 3.38 M parameters and 6.21 GFLOPs for 256 × 256 SAR–optical inputs. In leave-one-area-out transfer experiments, stratified few-shot adaptation increased the average F1 score from 0.4986 under zero-shot transfer to 0.7698. Grouped cross-continental and cross-sensor experiments further showed that direct transfer remains constrained under compound shifts in sensor characteristics, spatial resolution, landscape structure, and reference-label conventions. These findings indicate that SAF-CropNet combines strong within-region segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency with substantial gains from limited target-domain adaptation, while direct zero-shot generalization under severe compound domain shifts remains limited.
