record.title: Nested generative downscaling of passive microwave satellite data for navigation-scale Arctic sea ice forecasting
record.abstract: Rapid Arctic sea ice decline is increasing the accessibility of high-latitude shipping routes, but route-scale planning remains limited by the spatial resolution and ice-edge accuracy of Arctic sea ice concentration (SIC) forecasts. Coarse forecast products can smooth marginal ice zones, narrow straits, and fine-scale ice-edge features that are important for identifying navigable corridors during seasonal melt and freeze-up. Here we introduce IceNest, a navigation-oriented Arctic SIC forecasting framework that generates daily 6.25 km SIC forecasts up to 30 days ahead. IceNest couples a deep learning-based 25 km pan-Arctic forecast ensemble with a conditional diffusion model for residual downscaling. The forecasting ensemble uses the long OSI SAF SSM/I(S) passive microwave record together with historical environmental variables from ERA5, while the downscaling model learns AMSR-scale residual corrections from AMSR-series observations. Across 2020–2023, IceNest outperformed damped persistence and the evaluated Copernicus Climate Change Service seasonal forecast systems in terms of binary accuracy and integrated ice-edge error, with the largest gains during summer melt and autumn freeze-up. Route simulations along the Northeast Passage further yielded smaller errors in navigable-window timing and route distance than GloSea5/6 when evaluated against an AMSR2-based reference, highlighting the framework’s relevance to Arctic transit planning.
record.journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

record.title: PatchFusion: Resilient LiDAR-camera fusion for point cloud semantic segmentation in autonomous driving
record.abstract: LiDAR-camera fusion for point cloud semantic segmentation is essential for accurate and reliable 3D perception of autonomous driving systems. Contemporary LiDAR-camera fusion approaches predominantly integrate the pixel-level camera features located by projected points to augment the corresponding 3D points, which can be abstractly defined as point-pixel fusion strategy. Although such point-pixel fusion mode has been proved to be effective and widely used in practice, the strategy has two non-ignorable defects: (1) dependent on precise point-pixel projection correspondence, (2) limited by just using extremely little image information. Besides, the LiDAR-only inference in offline fusion fails to utilize the synchronously obtained images to achieve a dynamic fusion for 3D perception, while LiDAR-camera fusion inference in online fusion still encounters challenges of field of view (FoV) discrepancy between sensors. Moreover, the corruption robustness of LiDAR-camera fusion methods for 3D semantic segmentation, a crucial factor for the practical reliability of perception systems, has received limited attention. Thus, focusing on addressing above challenges, we develop the point-patch fusion mode, and construct PatchFusion framework as a systematic and promising solution to enhance performance and resilience of LiDAR-camera fusion perception in realistic and complex driving scenes. Specifically, in PatchFusion, we propose to leverage cross-attention mechanism to implement high-quality point-patch fusion by automatically searching what information should be highlighted or suppressed from the local patch of image, thereby alleviating the adverse effects of projection errors, maximizing the utilization of the high-density image information, and being more robust to the potential image corruptions. Besides, we integrate the strengths of offline and online fusion modes and propose a bidirectional cross-modality knowledge distillation strategy, aiming to further enhance the performance and robustness for predictions within and outside camera FoV. Finally, to bridge the research gap regarding the corruption robustness of LiDAR-camera fusion methods, we design a specialized dataset corruption suite for public multimodal datasets to simulate complex evaluation conditions by synthesizing projection noises and image corruptions. Extensive experiments on well-known datasets in autonomous driving (SemanticKITTI and nuScenes) demonstrate that PatchFusion can effectively improve the performance and resilience of LiDAR-camera fusion for 3D semantic segmentation on both clean and corrupted datasets. The relevant code will be available at https://github.com/sssssyf/PatchFusion.

record.title: Bridging the semantic gap in urban land use change detection with object-centric graph learning
record.abstract: A fundamental challenge in detecting land-use changes from high-resolution remote sensing images lies in the semantic gap between land cover and land use: imagery captures biophysical surface attributes through electromagnetic responses, but does not directly reveal socioeconomic functions. This gap is particularly pronounced in urban environments, where land-cover methods often fail to infer land-use semantics. Moreover, many deep learning methods rely on fixed-granularity image-scene analysis units, which exacerbate geometric and attribute uncertainties, causing imprecise boundaries, mixed-use ambiguity, and degraded performance in fine-grained urban land use change detection. To address these challenges, we propose a semantic-aware multi-spatial domain interaction network (SMDI-Net) that reformulates land-use change detection as a graph learning problem by modeling spatial structural differences of land-cover objects. By treating these objects as graph nodes and their topological relationships as edges, SMDI-Net establishes an explicit mapping between remote sensing imagery and land-use functional semantics, while precisely delineating change boundaries and maintaining semantic consistency within analysis units. Building upon this formulation, SMDI-Net further incorporates a multi-spatial domain interaction encoder to model land-cover dependencies across spatial scales, a hierarchical structural integration module to strengthen the identification of subtle structural transitions, and a discriminative feature enhancement module to characterize spatial structural shifts and semantic variation for refined change localization. Experiments on three datasets validate the superiority of SMDI-Net over seven state-of-the-art methods, achieving F1 scores of 93.32% for binary and 88.78% for multi-class change detection. These results show that SMDI-Net effectively alleviates geometric uncertainty and mixed-use ambiguity, offering a robust solution for fine-grained urban land-use monitoring. The code is available at https://github.com/Imp83121/SMDI-Net.

record.title: RamiGen: region-aware controllable diffusion with self-adaptive conditional evolution for instance-centric remote sensing object generation
record.abstract: Recent advances in deep generative modeling have substantially promoted remote sensing image generation, providing an effective solution for alleviating the expensive cost of data acquisition. Despite its effectiveness, most existing studies primarily focus on generic optical remote sensing scene synthesis involving large-scale natural elements, while the generation of instance-centric objects, such as aircraft, vehicles, ships, and military targets, remains underexplored. More importantly, previous generative models typically rely on macroscopic semantic guidance, image-level control, or coarse layout constraints, while neglecting the influence of complicated background and diverse resolutions, which often leads to geometric distortions, positional shifts, and physically implausible appearances in synthesized instance-centric remote sensing objects. To address these issues, we propose RamiGen, a Region-Aware Controllable Diffusion Model with Self-Adaptive Conditional Evolution for reference-guided instance-centric remote sensing object generation. Specifically, RamiGen leverages layouts as regional prompts and develops a Region-Aware Self-Adaptive Conditional Evolution Module (RA2CEM) to progressively evolve reference-derived coarse regional priors and capture spatially aligned, multi-dimensional fine-grained conditional features, which are collaboratively injected into the conditional guidance network of RamiGen to enhance object generation fidelity, spatial consistency, and physical plausibility. Meanwhile, a Spatial-Semantic Alignment Transformer (SSAFormer) is introduced into RamiGen to strengthen spatial-semantic token alignment for structural detail modeling during diffusion generative learning. Comprehensive experiments on optical and SAR remote sensing scenarios demonstrate that RamiGen achieves favorable overall performance against representative state-of-the-art methods, including AeroGen, OF-Diff, and GLIGEN. Specifically, RamiGen achieves FID scores of 37.586, 45.761, and 55.738 on DIOR, FRSMOD, and SARDet-100K, respectively, while obtaining YOLO Scores of 0.3212, 0.7319, and 0.2371, demonstrating superior generation fidelity and spatial-semantic consistency for densely or sparsely distributed small-object scenarios. Notably, samples generated by RamiGen achieve satisfactory downstream performance, highlighting its potential as a bimodal data generation foundation engine for remote sensing intelligent interpretation. The code is available at https://github.com/Bynus5/RamiGen-main-FRSMOD.

record.title: Submillimeter diffusion MRI using an in-plane segmented 3D multi-slab acquisition and denoiser-regularized reconstruction
record.abstract: Diffusion MRI (dMRI) enables brain connectivity mapping but is constrained by spatial resolution. Previous post-mortem studies have demonstrated the potential of submillimeter dMRI in enabling more precise delineations of curved and crossing white matter pathways. However, achieving such resolution in-vivo poses significant challenges due to the intrinsically low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Furthermore, for echo-planar imaging (EPI), large matrix sizes often require long echo spacing, readout duration, and echo times (TE), leading to significant image distortion, T2* blurring, and T2 signal decay. Here, we propose an acquisition and reconstruction framework to overcome these challenges. Based on numerical simulations, we employ in-plane segmented 3D multi-slab EPI that leverages the optimal SNR efficiency of 3D multi-slab imaging while reducing echo spacing, readout durations, and TE using in-plane segmentation. This approach minimizes distortion, improves image sharpness, and enhances SNR. Additionally, we develop a denoiser-regularized reconstruction to suppress noise while maintaining data fidelity, which reconstructs high-SNR images without introducing substantial blurring or bias. At 3T, we present 0.53–0.65 mm in-vivo data that reveal finer fiber architectures, reduced gyral bias, and improved U-fiber mapping compared to 1.22 mm data. At 7T, we acquire 0.61 mm data that show excellent agreement with high-resolution post-mortem dMRI, demonstrating robustness and high SNR at an ultra-high field. Our method is implemented using the open-source, scanner-agnostic framework Pulseq to facilitate broader adoption across scanner platforms to benefit a wider range of applications. These results establish our approach as a promising tool for high-resolution dMRI, advancing neuroanatomical investigations of white matter architecture.

record.title: Continuous-time causal distribution learning with identifiability for brain dynamic effective connectivity inference
record.abstract: Dynamic effective connectivity (dEC) analysis provides an approach for revealing the causal mechanism of information transmission in human brain. However, existing discrete-time dEC learning models suffer a mismatch between sampling and causal frequencies as well as low efficiency in data utilization. Based on a continuous-time dynamic causality distribution learning framework, we propose a dEC distribution learning model, which uses free energy principle to ensure more proper parameter learning than maximum likelihood estimation. Theoretically, the identifiability of the proposed model is proved, which guarantees the uniqueness of the learned dEC given the same data distribution. Results from the synthetic dataset show that the ability in both causality learning and time series reconstruction of the proposed model outperforms the comparison methods. The dEC results learned from the task functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data reveal the changing information transmission patterns in brain when dealing with picture-sentence matching tasks. Additionally, during the transition from resting state to task state, information flow in the brain’s dEC network becomes increasingly organized around the left supramarginal gyrus, a hub known for the language processing and information integration in parietal lobe. When applied to resting-state fMRI data on Alzheimer’s disease, the learned dEC patterns reveal distinct alterations in brain networks associated with Alzheimer’s disease. The results suggest that Alzheimer’s disease is associated with abnormalities not only in memory and emotion-related networks, but also in networks underlying executive control and visual integration. The source code of the proposed model are available at https://github.com/Yiding00/IDECD-CT.

record.title: MoCE-GAN: Mixture of Complexity Experts with generative adversarial networks for image restoration in sparse-view and limited-view photoacoustic tomography
record.abstract: Photoacoustic tomography (PAT) is a hybrid imaging modality that combines optical contrast with ultrasonic penetration depth for biomedical applications. Sparse-view and limited-view sampling strategies reduce acquisition time and system complexity but introduce reconstruction artifacts that degrade image quality and clinical utility. Although deep learning methods have advanced sparse-view PAT restoration, most rely on uniform architectures that allocate a fixed computational budget to every input sample, leaving them poorly matched to the varying degradation severity across samples. We propose MoCE-GAN, which couples a Mixture-of-Complexity-Experts (MoCE) generator—selecting experts according to sample-level degradation complexity via global feature statistics and a frequency embedding—with a PatchGAN discriminator that enforces local perceptual fidelity. Experiments on embryo numerical simulation, bone numerical simulation, in vivo mouse, and in vivo human datasets evaluate sparse-view settings with 16, 32, or 64 transducers and limited-view settings with 45°, 90°, or 180° angular coverage, depending on the acquisition geometry. Compared with four representative image-domain methods (PAT-ADN, FD-UNet, SA-UNet, GAID-PAT), MoCE-GAN raises PSNR over the best baseline by an average of 1.77 dB across the 16 dataset–configuration combinations under configuration-specific training, and by 2.10 dB under mixed training, where a single model covers all configurations and yields PSNR 0.24 dB lower on average than the configuration-specific models. SSIM and LPIPS are each best in most configurations. Beyond quantitative gains, restorations remain anatomically consistent under severe undersampling, supporting accelerated or reduced-view PAT acquisition scenarios.

record.title: Unsupervised denoising of diffusion-weighted images with bias and variance corrected noise modeling
record.abstract: Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) plays a vital role in both clinical diagnostics and neuroscience research. However, its inherently low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), especially under high diffusion weighting, substantially degrades image quality and impairs downstream analysis. Recent self-supervised and unsupervised denoising approaches have shown promising potential without requiring clean reference images. However, most of these methods neglect the non-Gaussian statistical characteristics of noise in magnitude dMRI data, leading to biased estimation and suboptimal optimization under heteroscedastic noise. To address this limitation, we propose two Rician noise-aware loss functions that explicitly account for these characteristics. One loss function is derived from the first-order moment of the Rician distribution for signal bias correction, while the other leverages the second-order moment to perform bias correction through squared-signal statistics. Each loss further incorporates adaptive weighting based on the signal-dependent Rician noise variance to address heteroscedasticity. The proposed objectives are instantiated within an image-specific, unsupervised Deep Image Prior (DIP) framework without modifying the network architecture. Comparisons with state-of-the-art denoising methods on simulated and in vivo dMRI data demonstrate that the proposed approach yields higher image quality and more reliable diffusion metrics. These results highlight the importance of explicitly accounting for Rician noise-induced bias and heteroscedasticity in magnitude-domain dMRI denoising. Code is available at https://github.com/XieJine/Rician-Moment-DIP.
